name: carrying a decision to its decider
from: A decision reaching the Chairperson or another decider as a bare yes/no line in chat — no context, no motivation, no options weighed, no consequences stated — so the decider must already hold the repository's state to rule on it, or rules on vibes.
to: A decision record the decider can rule on cold: the context forcing a choice, the options actually weighed, and the consequences of each, carrying nothing below the decider's own altitude. The decider does not have to open the repository to rule.
cost: The carrier's attention, spent writing out the options and consequences that were already implicit in whoever made the choice's own head — spent whether or not the decider ultimately agrees, which is the same cost analysing-a-requirement pays and for the same reason.
otherwise: Carriage happens ad hoc in chat, case by case, and the record of why a decision went one way lives nowhere a later reader can recover it.
